details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

cna.title: Incus before 6.0.7, 6.1.0 before 7.0.2, and 7.1.0 before 7.5.0 Authorization Bypass via GET /1.0/operations/{uuid}

descriptions.value: Incus before 6.0.7, 6.1.0 before 7.0.2, and 7.1.0 before 7.5.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in GET /1.0/operations/{uuid} that lets project-restricted clients read operations in other projects. Attackers holding a restricted certificate and a known operation UUID can retrieve command lines, environment secrets, websocket secrets, and trust enrolment tokens.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Incus before 6.0.7, 6.1.0 before 7.0.2, and 7.1.0 before 7.5.0 Authorization Bypass via GET /1.0/operations/{uuid}

cna.title: OpenBao 2.5.0 before 2.6.2 PKI allowed_ip_sans_cidr Bypass via CSR IP SANs

descriptions.value: OpenBao from 2.5.0 before 2.6.2 fails to enforce the PKI role allowed_ip_sans_cidr restriction on IP SANs taken from a CSR when use_csr_sans is enabled. Authenticated callers with sign permission can submit a CSR with an out-of-range IP SAN to pki/sign/<role> and obtain CA-signed certificates for unauthorized IPs.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenBao 2.5.0 before 2.6.2 PKI allowed_ip_sans_cidr Bypass via CSR IP SANs

cna.title: OpenBao 2.2.0 before 2.6.4 and 2.7.0 before 2.7.1 ACME EAB MAC Key Disclosure via Sanitized Configuration

descriptions.value: OpenBao 2.2.0 before 2.6.4 and 2.7.0 before 2.7.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that exposes the tls_acme_eab_mac_key value through the sys/config/state/sanitized endpoint. Callers of the sanitized configuration endpoint can retrieve the ACME External Account Binding MAC key used for TLS listener certificates, letting them bind to the operator's ACME account.

descriptions.description: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transfer

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenBao 2.2.0 before 2.6.4 and 2.7.0 before 2.7.1 ACME EAB MAC Key Disclosure via Sanitized Configuration

cna.title: OpenBao before 2.6.4 and 2.7.0 before 2.7.1 Role-Based Rate Limit Quota Bypass via Request Parsing

descriptions.value: OpenBao before 2.6.4 and 2.7.x before 2.7.1 contains a flaw in its rate limit quota subsystem where role resolution fails for requests with form-encoded bodies or forwarded certificates, so quota rules scoped to backend-specific roles are not enforced. Valid callers can repeatedly issue tokens without consuming the configured role-based rate limit budget.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: OpenBao before 2.6.4 and 2.7.0 before 2.7.1 Role-Based Rate Limit Quota Bypass via Request Parsing

cna.title: Mistune 3.2.1 before 3.3.0 CSS Injection via Figure Directive figwidth Option

descriptions.value: Mistune from 3.2.1 before 3.3.0 contains a CSS injection vulnerability that allows attackers controlling markdown input to inject arbitrary style declarations via the unvalidated figwidth option of the figure directive. Attackers can append declarations like background:url() to the rendered figure style attribute, forcing victim browsers to send requests to attacker servers and leak attribute values.

descriptions.description: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Mistune 3.2.1 before 3.3.0 CSS Injection via Figure Directive figwidth Option

cna.title: PhpSpreadsheet ODS Reader: Unbounded number-rows-repeated → CPU & Memory Exhaustion (DoS)

descriptions.description: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

descriptions.value: PhpSpreadsheet is a pure PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files. Prior to 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0, Ods::processTableRow in src/PhpSpreadsheet/Reader/Ods.php accepts an unbounded table:number-rows-repeated attribute from an ODS table row. When the row contains a value, the reader materializes a cell for every repetition without checking the spreadsheet row limit, so a small attacker-controlled ODS file can consume substantial CPU and memory and terminate the PHP worker. Column repetition is separately bounded and is not part of this vulnerability. This issue is fixed in versions 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0.

cna.title: PhpSpreadsheet: SSRF whitelist bypass via unre-validated HTTP redirect in Drawing::setPath external image loading

descriptions.value: PhpSpreadsheet is a pure PHP library for reading and writing spreadsheet files. Prior to 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0, Worksheet\Drawing::setPath validates only the initial external-image URL with setIsWhitelisted when setAllowExternalImages is enabled. The HTTP stream context permits PHP to follow a redirect without applying the callback to the redirected URL, so a permitted image host can redirect the server to an internal address and cause a blind GET request. The response body is not returned to the attacker because the reader validates the downloaded content as an image and removes the temporary file, but internal GET-driven endpoints, network reachability, and cloud metadata endpoints may be reached. This issue is fixed in versions 1.30.7, 2.1.19, 2.4.8, 3.10.8, and 5.10.0.

cna.title: Pylint: Arbitrary code execution via pickle deserialization of the stats cache in PYLINT_HOME

descriptions.value: Pylint is a static code analyser for Python. From 0.15.2 until 4.0.9, Pylint stores module statistics in predictable files under PYLINT_HOME and loads those files with pickle.load on a later run. An attacker who can write to a shared, group-writable, or otherwise untrusted cache directory can replace a stats cache with crafted serialized data, causing arbitrary code to execute with the privileges of the user who next runs Pylint. The default per-user cache is not normally writable by another user. This issue is fixed in version 4.0.9.

cna.title: GraphQL-core: Denial of service via comment tokens bypassing the parser's max_tokens limit

descriptions.description: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

descriptions.value: GraphQL-core is a Python port of the GraphQL.js reference implementation. From 3.2.3 until 3.2.12 and 3.3.0rc1, the parser's max_tokens limit in Parser.advance_lexer counts only non-comment tokens returned after Lexer.lookahead skips comments. Each skipped comment is still allocated as a Token and retained through token.next and token.prev, allowing a highly compressible comment-padded GraphQL document to pass a low token limit while consuming memory. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust worker memory before AST-based depth or complexity controls run. This issue is fixed in versions 3.2.12 and 3.3.0rc1.

cna.title: OCO-Server: Stored XSS through agent hostnames in command buttons

descriptions.description: CWE-83: Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes in a Web Page

descriptions.value: OCO-Server is a self-hosted endpoint management application for computer inventory, software deployment, and mobile device management. Prior to 1.2.1, `Html::commandButton()` in `lib/Html.class.php` embeds an action URL containing a stored computer hostname into a JavaScript string in an inline `onclick` handler, using `htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES)` only for HTML escaping. Browsers decode the HTML entities before interpreting the handler as JavaScript, allowing a crafted hostname to escape the string and execute script in an administrator's authenticated session when an affected command button is activated. `frontend/views/computer-details.php` passes `$computer->hostname` to this helper using `Computer::DEFAULT_COMPUTER_COMMANDS` in `lib/Models/Computer.class.php`, whose VNC, RDP, SSH, and Ping entries use `new_tab=false` and the vulnerable `window.location` branch. A remote attacker who possesses the shared `agent-registration-key` can use the `oco.agent.hello` handler in `frontend/api-agent.php` to store an unchecked hostname when `agent-self-registration-enabled` is enabled; self-registration is disabled by default. The vulnerable default command buttons require no custom command configuration. The injected script can abuse the administrator's privileges, including permission to deploy software jobs to managed computers. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.1.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A local attacker or untrusted guest virtual machine can exploit this vulnerability by transmitting network packets containing malformed checksum metadata into the IPv4 networking subsystem. This failure to validate checksum metadata can corrupt memory during packet handling, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the host, a system crash resulting in Denial of Service (DoS), or information disclosure of sensitive memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This IMPORTANT-severity flaw affects the Linux kernel as shipped in Red Hat products, including the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the kernels shipped in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. The IPv4 networking subsystem does not validate packet checksum metadata before completing a checksum: when a packet with a malformed checksum_start value enters the IPv4 stack, skb_checksum_help() can write out of bounds and corrupt the network header and other kernel memory (CWE-787). A local attacker or an untrusted guest virtual machine able to transmit such packets into an affected host could exploit this to crash the system (denial of service), disclose sensitive kernel memory, or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host. Red Hat tracks this flaw as a KEV active-exploit case. All currently tracked Red Hat product streams are marked affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible Red Hat product teams under delegated resolution. Red Hat's severity differs from the upstream assessment: Red Hat assigns a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (IMPORTANT, AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H), while the CVE.org record assigns 9.3 (CRITICAL, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H); the two assessments differ on the privileges-required metric.

notes.text: A flaw was found in dracut. A remote attacker on the adjacent network can exploit this vulnerability by providing specially crafted DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) options, such as a malicious hostname, to a system using dracut's legacy DHCP path. These options are improperly handled and written into temporary shell scripts without proper escaping, leading to command injection. This allows the attacker to achieve root code execution within the initramfs, potentially compromising the system's boot and network behavior.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: dracut: dracut: Root code execution via DHCP options command injection
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important vulnerability in dracut's legacy DHCP client script (`dhclient-script.sh`) that allows command injection. An attacker on the adjacent network can exploit this by providing specially crafted DHCP options, leading to root code execution within the initramfs. This primarily affects systems configured to use DHCP for network setup during the initial boot phase.

notes.text: A flaw was found in dracut. The die() error-handling function writes its message into a shell script under the initramfs emergency-hook directory without properly shell-quoting it. When the message contains data derived from the DHCP ROOT_PATH option, an attacker on the adjacent network who controls a rogue DHCP server can inject a command-substitution sequence that executes as root the next time dracut sources its emergency hook scripts during standard boot-failure handling.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: dracut: dracut: root code execution via unescaped error message written to sourced emergency hook script in die()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security rates this flaw's impact as Important. Exploitation requires an attacker-controlled or spoofed DHCP server on the same network segment as a system performing network boot (root=dhcp/netroot=dhcp), and for the DHCP-supplied ROOT_PATH value to fail dracut's netroot handler resolution -- both fully within an adjacent-network attacker's control. Reaching the point where the poisoned hook script is actually sourced depends on dracut's boot-failure handling reinvoking the emergency shell mechanism, which occurs by default when the netroot handler cannot be resolved. This is a separate code path from CVE-2026-6893, which patched modules.d/35network-legacy/dhclient-script.sh but did not modify dracut-lib.sh's die() function. Systems that do not perform network/PXE boot, or that do not rely on DHCP-supplied ROOT_PATH values, are not exposed to this issue.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in dracut. A remote attacker on the adjacent network can exploit this vulnerability by providing specially crafted DHCP options, such as a malicious root-path, next-server, or bootfile name, to a system using dracut's NetworkManager-based initrd network module. These options are improperly handled and written into a temporary shell script without proper escaping, leading to command injection. This allows the attacker to achieve root code execution within the initramfs during system boot.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important vulnerability in dracut's NetworkManager-based initrd network module (nm-run.sh) that allows command injection via crafted DHCP options. An attacker on the adjacent network can exploit this by acting as a DHCP server and providing specially crafted DHCP options, leading to root code execution within the initramfs. This affects systems configured to boot using dracut's network-manager module with a DHCP-derived netroot (for example, NFS-root configurations).

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `acl` package, specifically within its `libacl` pathname-based functions. A local attacker could exploit this vulnerability by using a symbolic link to replace a pathname component. This could allow the attacker to redirect access control list (ACL) read or write operations to arbitrary files or directories, leading to unauthorized manipulation of ACLs and ultimately local privilege escalation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this flaw as Important because a local attacker who controls any component of a pathname processed by a privileged process using libacl can redirect ACL operations to arbitrary files. Exploitation requires local access with the ability to create symlinks in a directory that a privileged program later processes with acl_get_file() or acl_set_file(). In default RHEL and OpenShift CoreOS configurations, standard file permission settings limit where unprivileged users can create symlinks, reducing the practical attack surface. Programs that operate on user-supplied paths with elevated privileges are most at risk.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's RDMA/rxe component. A local user could exploit a memory corruption vulnerability in the `free_rd_atomic_resources()` function by updating the `max_dest_rd_atomic` value before the old array is properly freed, leading to an out-of-bounds write. This issue can cause a system crash, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix OOB in free_rd_atomic_resources()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An OOB write in RDMA/RXE free_rd_atomic_resources can occur because qp attr max_dest_rd_atomic is updated before the old rd atomic resources array is freed. The free path then uses the new larger bound while walking the old smaller allocation, which can write past the kmalloc object and corrupt slab memory. The issue is not directly network reachable because the triggering operation is a local uverbs control path rather than inbound RDMA traffic.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A local attacker or untrusted guest virtual machine can exploit this vulnerability by transmitting network packets containing malformed checksum metadata into the IPv4 networking subsystem. This failure to validate checksum metadata can corrupt memory during packet handling, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the host, a system crash resulting in Denial of Service (DoS), or information disclosure of sensitive memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This IMPORTANT-severity flaw affects the Linux kernel as shipped in Red Hat products, including the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the kernels shipped in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. The IPv4 networking subsystem does not validate packet checksum metadata before completing a checksum: when a packet with a malformed checksum_start value enters the IPv4 stack, skb_checksum_help() can write out of bounds and corrupt the network header and other kernel memory (CWE-787). A local attacker or an untrusted guest virtual machine able to transmit such packets into an affected host could exploit this to crash the system (denial of service), disclose sensitive kernel memory, or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host. Red Hat tracks this flaw as a KEV active-exploit case. All currently tracked Red Hat product streams are marked affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible Red Hat product teams under delegated resolution. Red Hat's severity differs from the upstream assessment: Red Hat assigns a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (IMPORTANT, AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H), while the CVE.org record assigns 9.3 (CRITICAL, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H); the two assessments differ on the privileges-required metric.

notes.text:
The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

notes.text:
Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform is Red Hat's cloud computing
Kubernetes application platform solution designed for on-premise or private
cloud deployments.

This advisory contains the container images for Red Hat OpenShift Container
Platform 4.14.77. See the following advisory for the RPM packages for this
release:

https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:89837

Space precludes documenting all of the container images in this advisory.

shortly for this release, for details about these changes:

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.14/html/release_notes/

Security Fix(es):

* ca-certificates: Distrust eMudhra intermediate CA certificates due to
security concerns (CVE-2026-114406)
* kernel: netfilter: nft_set_pipapo_avx2: don't return non-matching entry
on expiry (CVE-2026-43114)

(CVE-2026-64564)

crafted regular expressions (CVE-2026-86145)

(CVE-2026-89161)
* pcre2: pcre2: Out-of-bounds write via crafted regular expression
(CVE-2026-103111)
* kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum (CVE-2026-99999)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS
score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE
page(s) listed in the References section.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A local attacker or untrusted guest virtual machine can exploit this vulnerability by transmitting network packets containing malformed checksum metadata into the IPv4 networking subsystem. This failure to validate checksum metadata can corrupt memory during packet handling, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the host, a system crash resulting in Denial of Service (DoS), or information disclosure of sensitive memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This IMPORTANT-severity flaw affects the Linux kernel as shipped in Red Hat products, including the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the kernels shipped in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. The IPv4 networking subsystem does not validate packet checksum metadata before completing a checksum: when a packet with a malformed checksum_start value enters the IPv4 stack, skb_checksum_help() can write out of bounds and corrupt the network header and other kernel memory (CWE-787). A local attacker or an untrusted guest virtual machine able to transmit such packets into an affected host could exploit this to crash the system (denial of service), disclose sensitive kernel memory, or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host. Red Hat tracks this flaw as a KEV active-exploit case. All currently tracked Red Hat product streams are marked affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible Red Hat product teams under delegated resolution. Red Hat's severity differs from the upstream assessment: Red Hat assigns a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (IMPORTANT, AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H), while the CVE.org record assigns 9.3 (CRITICAL, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H); the two assessments differ on the privileges-required metric.

notes.text:
The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform release 4.18.59 is now available with updates to packages and images that fix several bugs and add enhancements.

This release includes a security update for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.18.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score,

notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform is Red Hat's cloud computing Kubernetes application platform solution designed for on-premise or private cloud deployments.

This advisory contains the container images for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.18.59. See the following advisory for the RPM packages for this release:

https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:89724

Space precludes documenting all of the container images in this advisory. See the following Release Notes documentation, which will be updated shortly for this release, for details about these changes:

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.18/html/release_notes/

Security Fix(es):

* kernel: netfilter: nft_set_pipapo_avx2: don't return non-matching entry on expiry (CVE-2026-43114)
* acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions (CVE-2026-54369)
* openssh: OpenSSH sshd: Security bypass due to incorrect handling of forwarding and tunneling options (CVE-2026-59999)
* openssh: OpenSSH: Use-after-free vulnerability during host key re-exchange on the client side (CVE-2026-60002)
* kernel: sctp: don't free the ASCONF's own transport in DEL-IP processing (CVE-2026-64564)
* kernel: pppoe: reload header pointer after dev_hard_header() (CVE-2026-68121)
* kernel: ipv6: fix use-after-free in ip6_finish_output2() (CVE-2026-80792)
* pcre2: PCRE2: Out-of-bounds write allows arbitrary code execution via crafted regular expressions (CVE-2026-86145)
* pcre2: PCRE2: Memory corruption vulnerability in pcre2_jit_match (CVE-2026-89161)
* pcre2: pcre2: Out-of-bounds write via crafted regular expression (CVE-2026-103111)
* openssl: CMS AuthEnvelopedData Processing May Accept Forged Messages (CVE-2026-34182)
* openssl: AES-OCB IV Ignored on EVP_Cipher() Path (CVE-2026-45445)
* glib: off-by-one error in glib/gkeyfile.c via "g_key_file_get_locale_string_list" (CVE-2026-58014)
* openssh: OpenSSH: sftp client allows attacker to control downloaded file location (CVE-2026-59995)
* kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix OOB in free_rd_atomic_resources() (CVE-2026-80863)
* kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix responder UAF on IB_QP_MAX_DEST_RD_ATOMIC modify_qp (CVE-2026-80864)
* ca-certificates: Distrust eMudhra intermediate CA certificates due to security concerns (CVE-2026-114406)
* kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum (CVE-2026-99999)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenSSL. Applications that use the AES-OCB encryption method with a specific one-shot interface (EVP_Cipher()) will have their provided Initialization Vector (IV) silently discarded. This leads to the same internal cryptographic value being used repeatedly, which compromises the confidentiality of encrypted data. Additionally, this issue allows for the universal forgery of authentication tags, undermining the integrity of communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: openssl: AES-OCB IV Ignored on EVP_Cipher() Path
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is a Moderate severity flaw where applications utilizing the AES-OCB cipher through OpenSSL's EVP_Cipher() one-shot interface may silently discard the provided initialization vector (IV). This leads to nonce reuse, compromising confidentiality and enabling universal forgery of authentication tags. Red Hat products are primarily affected if they include or rely on third-party applications that specifically employ this less common and discouraged API usage with AES-OCB, as standard OpenSSL SSL/TLS implementations and applications using the recommended streaming AEAD API are not impacted.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `acl` package, specifically within its `libacl` pathname-based functions. A local attacker could exploit this vulnerability by using a symbolic link to replace a pathname component. This could allow the attacker to redirect access control list (ACL) read or write operations to arbitrary files or directories, leading to unauthorized manipulation of ACLs and ultimately local privilege escalation.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: acl: Symlink traversal privilege escalation via libacl functions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat rates this flaw as Important because a local attacker who controls any component of a pathname processed by a privileged process using libacl can redirect ACL operations to arbitrary files. Exploitation requires local access with the ability to create symlinks in a directory that a privileged program later processes with acl_get_file() or acl_set_file(). In default RHEL and OpenShift CoreOS configurations, standard file permission settings limit where unprivileged users can create symlinks, reducing the practical attack surface. Programs that operate on user-supplied paths with elevated privileges are most at risk.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's RDMA/rxe component. A local user could exploit a memory corruption vulnerability in the `free_rd_atomic_resources()` function by updating the `max_dest_rd_atomic` value before the old array is properly freed, leading to an out-of-bounds write. This issue can cause a system crash, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix OOB in free_rd_atomic_resources()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An OOB write in RDMA/RXE free_rd_atomic_resources can occur because qp attr max_dest_rd_atomic is updated before the old rd atomic resources array is freed. The free path then uses the new larger bound while walking the old smaller allocation, which can write past the kmalloc object and corrupt slab memory. The issue is not directly network reachable because the triggering operation is a local uverbs control path rather than inbound RDMA traffic.
notes.title: Statement

1. Create a configuration file in /etc/modprobe.d to disable loading of the module:

notes.text: A flaw was found in PCRE2. An out-of-bounds write vulnerability exists in the `pcre2_dfa_match` function due to improper size checking when reusing cached workspace blocks. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted regular expression or a recursive pattern in conjunction with a small heap limit. This could lead to data corruption or potentially arbitrary code execution, compromising the integrity and availability of the system.

To mitigate this Improper Protection of Alternate Path vulnerability, ensure that secondary execution branches—such as the reuse of cached memory workspaces—enforce the exact same size and boundary checks as the primary memory allocation paths. notes.text: A flaw was found in PCRE2, a library for processing regular expressions. The `pcre2_jit_match` function, which handles just-in-time (JIT) compilation for regular expressions, incorrectly manages memory when processing certain inputs. This memory corruption vulnerability could allow a local attacker to cause the application to crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially execute unauthorized code.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important memory corruption vulnerability in PCRE2's JIT compiler. An attacker could exploit a flaw in `pcre2_jit_match` when a previously copied subject is passed as context, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or denial of service. The high attack complexity and local attack vector reduce the overall risk, but the widespread use of PCRE2 and the potential for severe impact warrant the Important classification.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A local attacker or untrusted guest virtual machine can exploit this vulnerability by transmitting network packets containing malformed checksum metadata into the IPv4 networking subsystem. This failure to validate checksum metadata can corrupt memory during packet handling, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the host, a system crash resulting in Denial of Service (DoS), or information disclosure of sensitive memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This IMPORTANT-severity flaw affects the Linux kernel as shipped in Red Hat products, including the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the kernels shipped in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. The IPv4 networking subsystem does not validate packet checksum metadata before completing a checksum: when a packet with a malformed checksum_start value enters the IPv4 stack, skb_checksum_help() can write out of bounds and corrupt the network header and other kernel memory (CWE-787). A local attacker or an untrusted guest virtual machine able to transmit such packets into an affected host could exploit this to crash the system (denial of service), disclose sensitive kernel memory, or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host. Red Hat tracks this flaw as a KEV active-exploit case. All currently tracked Red Hat product streams are marked affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible Red Hat product teams under delegated resolution. Red Hat's severity differs from the upstream assessment: Red Hat assigns a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (IMPORTANT, AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H), while the CVE.org record assigns 9.3 (CRITICAL, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H); the two assessments differ on the privileges-required metric.

notes.text:
The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

notes.text:
Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform is Red Hat's cloud computing Kubernetes application platform solution designed for on-premise or private cloud deployments.

This advisory contains the container images for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.16.74. See the following advisory for the RPM packages for this release:

https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHSA-2026:89713

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.16/html/release_notes/

Security Fix(es):

* kernel: netfilter: nft_set_pipapo_avx2: don't return non-matching entry on expiry (CVE-2026-43114)
* kernel: sctp: don't free the ASCONF's own transport in DEL-IP processing (CVE-2026-64564)
* kernel: pppoe: reload header pointer after dev_hard_header() (CVE-2026-68121)
* kernel: ipv6: fix use-after-free in ip6_finish_output2() (CVE-2026-80792)
* kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix OOB in free_rd_atomic_resources() (CVE-2026-80863)
* kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix responder UAF on IB_QP_MAX_DEST_RD_ATOMIC modify_qp (CVE-2026-80864)
* ca-certificates: Distrust eMudhra intermediate CA certificates due to security concerns (CVE-2026-114406)
* kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum (CVE-2026-99999)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's netfilter component, specifically within the `nft_set_pipapo_avx2` AVX2 matching functions. This vulnerability occurs when a `pipapo` set with an 'ipv4 . port' key is reloaded. Due to incorrect masking, the system may erroneously identify non-matching elements as duplicates, leading to data integrity issues and unexpected behavior. A remote attacker could potentially exploit this to cause a denial of service or impact data integrity.

This issue primarily impacts Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and 10 systems configured to utilize AVX2 instructions for netfilter set processing.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's RDMA/rxe component. A local user could exploit a memory corruption vulnerability in the `free_rd_atomic_resources()` function by updating the `max_dest_rd_atomic` value before the old array is properly freed, leading to an out-of-bounds write. This issue can cause a system crash, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix OOB in free_rd_atomic_resources()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An OOB write in RDMA/RXE free_rd_atomic_resources can occur because qp attr max_dest_rd_atomic is updated before the old rd atomic resources array is freed. The free path then uses the new larger bound while walking the old smaller allocation, which can write past the kmalloc object and corrupt slab memory. The issue is not directly network reachable because the triggering operation is a local uverbs control path rather than inbound RDMA traffic.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A local attacker or untrusted guest virtual machine can exploit this vulnerability by transmitting network packets containing malformed checksum metadata into the IPv4 networking subsystem. This failure to validate checksum metadata can corrupt memory during packet handling, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the host, a system crash resulting in Denial of Service (DoS), or information disclosure of sensitive memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This IMPORTANT-severity flaw affects the Linux kernel as shipped in Red Hat products, including the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the kernels shipped in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. The IPv4 networking subsystem does not validate packet checksum metadata before completing a checksum: when a packet with a malformed checksum_start value enters the IPv4 stack, skb_checksum_help() can write out of bounds and corrupt the network header and other kernel memory (CWE-787). A local attacker or an untrusted guest virtual machine able to transmit such packets into an affected host could exploit this to crash the system (denial of service), disclose sensitive kernel memory, or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host. Red Hat tracks this flaw as a KEV active-exploit case. All currently tracked Red Hat product streams are marked affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible Red Hat product teams under delegated resolution. Red Hat's severity differs from the upstream assessment: Red Hat assigns a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (IMPORTANT, AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H), while the CVE.org record assigns 9.3 (CRITICAL, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H); the two assessments differ on the privileges-required metric.

notes.text:
The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

notes.text:
Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform is Red Hat's cloud computing Kubernetes application platform solution designed for on-premise or private cloud deployments.

This advisory contains the container images for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.19.53. See the following advisory for the RPM packages for this release:

https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2026:89649

Space precludes documenting all of the container images in this advisory. See the following Release Notes documentation, which will be updated shortly for this release, for details about these changes:

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.19/html/release_notes/

Security Fix(es):

* openssl: Heap Use-After-Free in OpenSSL PKCS7_verify() (CVE-2026-45447)
* openssh: OpenSSH sshd: Security bypass due to incorrect handling of forwarding and tunneling options (CVE-2026-59999)
* kernel: sctp: don't free the ASCONF's own transport in DEL-IP processing (CVE-2026-64564)
* kernel: ipv6: fix use-after-free in ip6_finish_output2() (CVE-2026-80792)
* pcre2: PCRE2: Out-of-bounds write allows arbitrary code execution via crafted regular expressions (CVE-2026-86145)
* pcre2: PCRE2: Memory corruption vulnerability in pcre2_jit_match (CVE-2026-89161)
* pcre2: pcre2: Out-of-bounds write via crafted regular expression (CVE-2026-103111)
* gnutls: gnutls: Information disclosure via heap overread in RSA key exchange (CVE-2026-5260)
* bind: bind9: Incorrect acceptance of NSEC3 records (CVE-2026-10723)
* openssl: CMS AuthEnvelopedData Processing May Accept Forged Messages (CVE-2026-34182)
* openssl: Unbounded Memory Growth in the QUIC PATH_CHALLENGE Handler (CVE-2026-34183)
* openssl: AES-OCB IV Ignored on EVP_Cipher() Path (CVE-2026-45445)
* openssh: OpenSSH: sftp client allows attacker to control downloaded file location (CVE-2026-59995)
* kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix OOB in free_rd_atomic_resources() (CVE-2026-80863)
* kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix responder UAF on IB_QP_MAX_DEST_RD_ATOMIC modify_qp (CVE-2026-80864)
* ca-certificates: Distrust eMudhra intermediate CA certificates due to security concerns (CVE-2026-114406)
* kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum (CVE-2026-99999)

A remote attacker, by sending an extremely short premaster secret during an RSA key exchange to a server using an RSA key backed by a PKCS#11 token, could trigger a short heap overread. notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's RDMA/rxe component. A local user could exploit a memory corruption vulnerability in the `free_rd_atomic_resources()` function by updating the `max_dest_rd_atomic` value before the old array is properly freed, leading to an out-of-bounds write. This issue can cause a system crash, resulting in a denial of service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix OOB in free_rd_atomic_resources()
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An OOB write in RDMA/RXE free_rd_atomic_resources can occur because qp attr max_dest_rd_atomic is updated before the old rd atomic resources array is freed. The free path then uses the new larger bound while walking the old smaller allocation, which can write past the kmalloc object and corrupt slab memory. The issue is not directly network reachable because the triggering operation is a local uverbs control path rather than inbound RDMA traffic.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A local attacker or untrusted guest virtual machine can exploit this vulnerability by transmitting network packets containing malformed checksum metadata into the IPv4 networking subsystem. This failure to validate checksum metadata can corrupt memory during packet handling, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the host, a system crash resulting in Denial of Service (DoS), or information disclosure of sensitive memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This IMPORTANT-severity flaw affects the Linux kernel as shipped in Red Hat products, including the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the kernels shipped in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. The IPv4 networking subsystem does not validate packet checksum metadata before completing a checksum: when a packet with a malformed checksum_start value enters the IPv4 stack, skb_checksum_help() can write out of bounds and corrupt the network header and other kernel memory (CWE-787). A local attacker or an untrusted guest virtual machine able to transmit such packets into an affected host could exploit this to crash the system (denial of service), disclose sensitive kernel memory, or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host. Red Hat tracks this flaw as a KEV active-exploit case. All currently tracked Red Hat product streams are marked affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible Red Hat product teams under delegated resolution. Red Hat's severity differs from the upstream assessment: Red Hat assigns a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (IMPORTANT, AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H), while the CVE.org record assigns 9.3 (CRITICAL, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H); the two assessments differ on the privileges-required metric.

The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

notes.text:
Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform is Red Hat's cloud computing Kubernetes application platform solution designed for on-premise or private cloud deployments.

This advisory contains the container images for Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.20.44. See the following advisory for the RPM packages for this release:

https://access.redhat.com/errata/RHBA-2026:89332

Space precludes documenting all of the container images in this advisory. See the following Release Notes documentation, which will be updated shortly for this release, for details about these changes:

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/openshift_container_platform/4.20/html/release_notes/

Security Fix(es):

* openssl: Heap Use-After-Free in OpenSSL PKCS7_verify() (CVE-2026-45447)
* openssh: OpenSSH sshd: Security bypass due to incorrect handling of forwarding and tunneling options (CVE-2026-59999)
* kernel: sctp: don't free the ASCONF's own transport in DEL-IP processing (CVE-2026-64564)
* kernel: ipv6: fix use-after-free in ip6_finish_output2() (CVE-2026-80792)
* pcre2: PCRE2: Out-of-bounds write allows arbitrary code execution via crafted regular expressions (CVE-2026-86145)
* pcre2: PCRE2: Memory corruption vulnerability in pcre2_jit_match (CVE-2026-89161)
* pcre2: pcre2: Out-of-bounds write via crafted regular expression (CVE-2026-103111)
* gnutls: gnutls: Information disclosure via heap overread in RSA key exchange (CVE-2026-5260)
* bind: bind9: Incorrect acceptance of NSEC3 records (CVE-2026-10723)
* openssl: CMS AuthEnvelopedData Processing May Accept Forged Messages (CVE-2026-34182)
* openssl: Unbounded Memory Growth in the QUIC PATH_CHALLENGE Handler (CVE-2026-34183)
* gnutls: gnutls: Security bypass due to incorrect name constraint handling (CVE-2026-42011)
* gnutls: gnutls: Certificate validation bypass due to improper handling of URI and SRV SANs (CVE-2026-42012)
* gnutls: gnutls: Certificate validation bypass due to oversized Subject Alternative Name (CVE-2026-42013)
* openssl: AES-OCB IV Ignored on EVP_Cipher() Path (CVE-2026-45445)
* openssh: OpenSSH: sftp client allows attacker to control downloaded file location (CVE-2026-59995)
* kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix OOB in free_rd_atomic_resources() (CVE-2026-80863)
* kernel: RDMA/rxe: Fix responder UAF on IB_QP_MAX_DEST_RD_ATOMIC modify_qp (CVE-2026-80864)
* ca-certificates: Distrust eMudhra intermediate CA certificates due to security concerns (CVE-2026-114406)
* kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum (CVE-2026-99999)

A remote attacker, by sending an extremely short premaster secret during an RSA key exchange to a server using an RSA key backed by a PKCS#11 token, could trigger a short heap overread. This memory corruption vulnerability could lead to information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: gnutls: gnutls: Information disclosure via heap overread in RSA key exchange
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security rates this vulnerability as Moderate severity because exploitation requires a specialized server setup where RSA key exchange is negotiated using a private key hosted on a PKCS#11 token. In standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, system-wide crypto policies prioritize forward-secret (EC)DHE cipher suites, and PKCS#11 hardware tokens are not configured by default. Furthermore, the issue only triggers a bounded heap overread, resulting in limited information disclosure rather than arbitrary code execution.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenSSL's QUIC PATH_CHALLENGE handler. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by flooding a QUIC client or server with specially crafted PATH_CHALLENGE frames. This leads to unbounded memory allocation within the local QUIC stack, as the system continuously allocates PATH_RESPONSE frames without them being acknowledged. The primary consequence is a Denial of Service (DoS), causing the affected application to terminate abnormally due to memory exhaustion.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A Moderate severity flaw exists in the QUIC PATH_CHALLENGE handler, allowing a remote attacker to exhaust heap memory of a QUIC client or server. By flooding the local QUIC stack with PATH_CHALLENGE frames, a malicious peer can trigger unbounded memory allocation, leading to a denial of service for applications utilizing the vulnerable QUIC implementation.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gnutls. When validating certificates, an oversized Subject Alternative Name (SAN) could cause the validation process to incorrectly fall back to checking the Common Name (CN) field. This could allow a remote attacker to bypass proper certificate validation, potentially leading to spoofing or man-in-the-middle attacks.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: gnutls: gnutls: Certificate validation bypass due to oversized Subject Alternative Name
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact across affected Red Hat products because successful exploitation requires an active man-in-the-middle network position as well as a certificate issued by a trusted authority matching the target hostname's Common Name. Although TLS clients using GnuTLS on Red Hat Enterprise Linux and OpenShift are susceptible to improper certificate acceptance under these conditions, modern certificate authorities rarely issue certificates that omit valid Subject Alternative Names, substantially restricting practical threat vectors. Applications functioning exclusively as TLS servers or utilizing alternative cryptographic libraries like OpenSSL are not exposed to this flaw.

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenSSL. Applications that use the AES-OCB encryption method with a specific one-shot interface (EVP_Cipher()) will have their provided Initialization Vector (IV) silently discarded. This leads to the same internal cryptographic value being used repeatedly, which compromises the confidentiality of encrypted data. Additionally, this issue allows for the universal forgery of authentication tags, undermining the integrity of communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: openssl: AES-OCB IV Ignored on EVP_Cipher() Path
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is a Moderate severity flaw where applications utilizing the AES-OCB cipher through OpenSSL's EVP_Cipher() one-shot interface may silently discard the provided initialization vector (IV). This leads to nonce reuse, compromising confidentiality and enabling universal forgery of authentication tags. Red Hat products are primarily affected if they include or rely on third-party applications that specifically employ this less common and discouraged API usage with AES-OCB, as standard OpenSSL SSL/TLS implementations and applications using the recommended streaming AEAD API are not impacted.
notes.title: Statement

The vulnerability specifically affects applications utilizing OpenSSL PKCS#7 APIs, while those using CMS APIs are not impacted.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A local attacker or untrusted guest virtual machine can exploit this vulnerability by transmitting network packets containing malformed checksum metadata into the IPv4 networking subsystem. This failure to validate checksum metadata can corrupt memory during packet handling, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the host, a system crash resulting in Denial of Service (DoS), or information disclosure of sensitive memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This IMPORTANT-severity flaw affects the Linux kernel as shipped in Red Hat products, including the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the kernels shipped in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. The IPv4 networking subsystem does not validate packet checksum metadata before completing a checksum: when a packet with a malformed checksum_start value enters the IPv4 stack, skb_checksum_help() can write out of bounds and corrupt the network header and other kernel memory (CWE-787). A local attacker or an untrusted guest virtual machine able to transmit such packets into an affected host could exploit this to crash the system (denial of service), disclose sensitive kernel memory, or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host. Red Hat tracks this flaw as a KEV active-exploit case. All currently tracked Red Hat product streams are marked affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible Red Hat product teams under delegated resolution. Red Hat's severity differs from the upstream assessment: Red Hat assigns a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (IMPORTANT, AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H), while the CVE.org record assigns 9.3 (CRITICAL, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H); the two assessments differ on the privileges-required metric.

notes.text:
The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

notes.text: A flaw was found in libgnutls. A remote attacker, by sending an extremely short premaster secret during an RSA key exchange to a server using an RSA key backed by a PKCS#11 token, could trigger a short heap overread. This memory corruption vulnerability could lead to information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: gnutls: gnutls: Information disclosure via heap overread in RSA key exchange
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security rates this vulnerability as Moderate severity because exploitation requires a specialized server setup where RSA key exchange is negotiated using a private key hosted on a PKCS#11 token. In standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments, system-wide crypto policies prioritize forward-secret (EC)DHE cipher suites, and PKCS#11 hardware tokens are not configured by default. Furthermore, the issue only triggers a bounded heap overread, resulting in limited information disclosure rather than arbitrary code execution.

notes.text: A flaw was found in OpenSSL's QUIC PATH_CHALLENGE handler. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by flooding a QUIC client or server with specially crafted PATH_CHALLENGE frames. This leads to unbounded memory allocation within the local QUIC stack, as the system continuously allocates PATH_RESPONSE frames without them being acknowledged. The primary consequence is a Denial of Service (DoS), causing the affected application to terminate abnormally due to memory exhaustion.

notes.text: openssl: Unbounded Memory Growth in the QUIC PATH_CHALLENGE Handler
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A Moderate severity flaw exists in the QUIC PATH_CHALLENGE handler, allowing a remote attacker to exhaust heap memory of a QUIC client or server. By flooding the local QUIC stack with PATH_CHALLENGE frames, a malicious peer can trigger unbounded memory allocation, leading to a denial of service for applications utilizing the vulnerable QUIC implementation.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gnutls. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by presenting a specially crafted certificate that contains Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) or Service (SRV) Subject Alternative Names (SANs). This could cause the certificate validation process to incorrectly fall back to checking DNS hostnames against the Common Name (CN), potentially allowing the attacker to spoof legitimate services or intercept sensitive information.

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Moderate severity because exploitation requires an active man-in-the-middle position or tricking a client into connecting to a rogue endpoint, along with obtaining a validly signed certificate containing specialized SAN fields. While GnuTLS is widely deployed across Red Hat products as a core cryptographic library, the impact is limited to hostname verification spoofing under specific certificate configurations. The issue does not permit remote code execution or direct compromise of the underlying system.

notes.text: A flaw was found in gnutls. When validating certificates, an oversized Subject Alternative Name (SAN) could cause the validation process to incorrectly fall back to checking the Common Name (CN) field. This could allow a remote attacker to bypass proper certificate validation, potentially leading to spoofing or man-in-the-middle attacks.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: gnutls: gnutls: Certificate validation bypass due to oversized Subject Alternative Name
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact across affected Red Hat products because successful exploitation requires an active man-in-the-middle network position as well as a certificate issued by a trusted authority matching the target hostname's Common Name. Although TLS clients using GnuTLS on Red Hat Enterprise Linux and OpenShift are susceptible to improper certificate acceptance under these conditions, modern certificate authorities rarely issue certificates that omit valid Subject Alternative Names, substantially restricting practical threat vectors. Applications functioning exclusively as TLS servers or utilizing alternative cryptographic libraries like OpenSSL are not exposed to this flaw.

Limit exposure by preventing untrusted user input from directly controlling PCRE2 regular expressions, and strictly avoid utilizing recursive matching patterns when operating under a low heap limit. Apply a defense-in-depth strategy by validating all inputs comprehensively.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel. A local attacker or untrusted guest virtual machine can exploit this vulnerability by transmitting network packets containing malformed checksum metadata into the IPv4 networking subsystem. This failure to validate checksum metadata can corrupt memory during packet handling, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the host, a system crash resulting in Denial of Service (DoS), or information disclosure of sensitive memory.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This IMPORTANT-severity flaw affects the Linux kernel as shipped in Red Hat products, including the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux and the kernels shipped in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS. The IPv4 networking subsystem does not validate packet checksum metadata before completing a checksum: when a packet with a malformed checksum_start value enters the IPv4 stack, skb_checksum_help() can write out of bounds and corrupt the network header and other kernel memory (CWE-787). A local attacker or an untrusted guest virtual machine able to transmit such packets into an affected host could exploit this to crash the system (denial of service), disclose sensitive kernel memory, or potentially execute arbitrary code on the host. Red Hat tracks this flaw as a KEV active-exploit case. All currently tracked Red Hat product streams are marked affected, and fixes are being pursued by the responsible Red Hat product teams under delegated resolution. Red Hat's severity differs from the upstream assessment: Red Hat assigns a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.8 (IMPORTANT, AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H), while the CVE.org record assigns 9.3 (CRITICAL, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H); the two assessments differ on the privileges-required metric.

notes.text:
The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Intel(R) Processors within Ring 0, affecting the kernel, hypervisor, and bare metal operating systems. Improper handling of values may allow an authorized adversary with privileged user access to perform a local, high-complexity attack. This can lead to an escalation of privilege, potentially resulting in high impact to the confidentiality and integrity of the system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: hypervisor: Intel Processors: Privilege escalation in Ring 0 via improper value handling
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
Red Hat is aware of a hardware vulnerability affecting some Intel processors that could allow a local attacker who already has privileged access to escalate privileges by exploiting improper handling of internal processor values during Ring 0 execution. In the most severe case, this could allow a privileged workload running inside a virtual machine to escalate access into the underlying hypervisor. Exploitation requires local access, existing privileged access, and a high degree of attack complexity, including detailed knowledge of the processor's internal behavior.

Red Hat products that provide workload isolation using a hypervisor, such as Red Hat OpenShift sandboxed containers (which uses Kata Containers), are assessed as Important severity because of the potential impact on isolation between different tenants' workloads if the underlying processor is vulnerable and has not been updated.

notes.text: A flaw was found in libpcap. The Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) interpreter in libpcap does not properly validate register indexes in BPF instructions. A local attacker could craft a malicious filter program to trigger an out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability. This could allow the attacker to read and write arbitrary operating system process memory, potentially leading to information disclosure or arbitrary code execution.

This could result in arbitrary read and write operations within the OS process memory.

notes.text: A flaw was found in curl's cookie parsing logic. A malicious HTTP server can exploit this by setting 'super cookies' that bypass the Public Suffix List check. notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate: Red Hat rates this flaw Moderate (CVSS 6.5) compared to CISA's Critical (9.1). The scoring difference is due to two factors: first, exploitation requires the victim's curl to connect using a trailing-dot hostname (e.g., https://example.co.uk.), a format that is uncommon in practice and incompatible with TLS SNI; second, the direct impact is cookie injection into outbound requests — not exfiltration of victim data to the attacker. Red Hat products that use curl for HTTP communication are affected, but the trailing-dot precondition significantly limits real-world exploitability. This flaw has not been shown to enable impacts beyond session integrity modification.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the URI component for Perl. This vulnerability occurs because the `nameprep` function, responsible for encoding hostnames, does not properly normalize Unicode characters. As a result, a hostname that is not in a standard Unicode form (non-NFC) can be encoded into a non-standard label. This discrepancy can lead to a situation where security checks, such as allow lists or Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) filters, may incorrectly process hostnames, potentially allowing an attacker to bypass security restrictions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: URI: URI (for Perl): Security bypass due to incorrect hostname encoding via missing Unicode normalization
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is a pure logic bypass (CWE-1289), not a memory safety vulnerability. Successful exploitation requires a very specific, multi-condition application pattern: (1) the application accepts a URL from untrusted network input; (2) it parses the URL with `URI->new()`; (3) it extracts the hostname via `->host()` and uses it for a security decision (e.g., SSRF filtering); and (4) it separately fetches the URL with a client that performs correct IDNA normalization. Only when all four conditions are simultaneously true can an attacker bypass the security control.

notes.text: A flaw was found in `sshd`, the OpenSSH server daemon. When `DisableForwarding=yes` is configured to prevent network traffic forwarding, it incorrectly fails to take precedence over `PermitTunnel=yes`. This allows a remote attacker to bypass intended security restrictions and establish a tunnel, potentially leading to unauthorized network access or circumvention of security policies, even when forwarding is explicitly disabled.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: openssh: OpenSSH sshd: Security bypass due to incorrect handling of forwarding and tunneling options
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Moderate severity flaw in OpenSSH `sshd` allows `PermitTunnel=yes` to override `DisableForwarding=yes`, potentially bypassing intended security controls. In Red Hat environments where `DisableForwarding` is used to restrict SSH session capabilities, an attacker who compromises a user's session could still establish a tunnel, leading to unauthorized network access or data exfiltration. This bypass occurs even when administrators explicitly attempt to prevent forwarding, though `PermitTunnel` is not enabled by default.

notes.text: A flaw was found in libevent. The evhttp_decode_uri_internal function in http.c decodes percent-encoded %00 bytes into literal NUL characters without rejecting them, allowing an attacker to craft a URI such as /admin/secret%00.jpg where extension-based access checks see .jpg but the server processes /admin/secret, bypassing path-based access controls. Additionally, evhttp_header_is_valid_value accepts obsolete HTTP header line folding (CRLF followed by SP/HT), which RFC 9112 states new implementations should reject, creating a header injection vector in proxy chains where the frontend rejects obs-fold but libevent accepts it. This could lead to access control bypass, header injection, or request smuggling.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Open vSwitch component of the Linux kernel. This vulnerability arises from an underflow condition when handling Generic Segmentation Offload (GSO) packets in userspace. A length calculation error can lead to a buffer underflow when data is processed by the `skb_zerocopy()` function. This issue could result in memory corruption, potentially leading to a denial of service or other unpredictable system behavior.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: openvswitch: fix GSO userspace truncation underflow
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: The Linux kernel packages (kernel and kernel-rt) shipped in Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and other Red Hat products that reuse the kernel are affected by this IMPORTANT severity flaw in the Open vSwitch datapath code. When an Open vSwitch flow applies the packet truncation action (OVS_ACTION_ATTR_TRUNC) to a packet that is later segmented for a Generic Segmentation Offload (GSO) userspace action, the kernel reuses a truncation delta computed against the original, larger packet for each smaller segment. A segment can then reach queue_userspace_packet() with a truncation length greater than the segment length, and the underflowed length passed to skb_zerocopy() causes an out-of-bounds access and kernel memory corruption. The likely consequences are a kernel crash, denial of service, or other unpredictable system behavior. Exploitation requires local access and the ability to trigger the affected Open vSwitch userspace action path under specific, complex conditions, which is reflected in the Red Hat rating of 7.0 IMPORTANT (CVSS 3.1: AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H). This differs from the upstream CVE record, which assigns 9.8 CRITICAL using a network attack vector; Red Hat rates the flaw lower because the verified attack path is local and requires high attack complexity and privileges rather than unauthenticated remote exploitation. A fix is being pursued for the affected Red Hat product streams. The Red Hat Enterprise Linux for NVIDIA kernel is not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in that build.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `drm/vmwgfx` component of the Linux kernel. An integer overflow vulnerability exists in the `vmw_shader_define()` function due to improper validation of user-supplied shader window size and offset. When the offset value is close to its maximum, an unsigned addition can wrap around, causing the size check to pass incorrectly. This allows an unbounded offset to be used, which could lead to memory corruption and potentially privilege escalation or denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: drm/vmwgfx: use check_add_overflow for shader size+offset bound
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel drm/vmwgfx driver, which Red Hat Product Security rates as IMPORTANT (CVSS 7.0, CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H). The vmw_shader_define() function validates a user-supplied shader window against its backing buffer using an unsigned addition of size and offset. Because drm_vmw_shader_create_arg::offset is a 64-bit user-controlled value, an offset near U64_MAX causes the addition to wrap around, so the resulting small value incorrectly passes the bounds check. The unbounded offset is then stored in res->guest_memory_offset and forwarded to the host SVGA shader-create commands. A local unprivileged attacker with access to the vmwgfx DRM device, such as within a guest virtual machine using VMware graphics, could exploit this integer overflow to cause memory corruption, potentially leading to privilege escalation or denial of service; successful exploitation is judged to require high attack complexity. Currently affected products include the Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10 kernels (kernel and kernel-rt) and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, for which fixes are being pursued. Several older update streams (RHEL 7 ELS, RHEL 8.4, 8.6, and 8.8 z streams, and RHEL 9.2.0.z) are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in those kernels.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's AF_IUCV (Advanced Program-to-Program Communication over IUCV) network protocol implementation. The `afiucv_hs_rcv()` function, responsible for receiving frames, does not properly filter incoming frames based on the ingress network device. This oversight allows a local attacker with specific network capabilities or a host on the same HiperSockets segment to send specially crafted frames. Successful exploitation can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting the accept-queue, injecting data into existing sockets, and disrupting established connections.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: kernel: net/iucv: filter frames in afiucv_hs_rcv() by ingress device
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw rated IMPORTANT by Red Hat Product Security was found in the Linux kernel's AF_IUCV protocol implementation, used for the z/VM IUCV and HiperSockets transports on the s390x (IBM Z) architecture. The afiucv_hs_rcv() receive path selected a target socket from the global socket list by matching only the four 8-byte name fields in the frame's transport header, without checking the network device the frame arrived on. As a result, a frame received on any network device could be delivered to an AF_IUCV socket bound to a different device or to the classic z/VM IUCV transport. A local attacker holding only the CAP_NET_RAW capability inside an unprivileged user and network namespace could send a raw ETH_P_AF_IUCV frame on its own loopback device and have it matched against sockets in the initial network namespace; similarly, a host on the same shared HiperSockets segment could direct frames at sockets bound to a different HiperSockets device. Successful exploitation could exhaust a listening socket's accept queue (denial of service), inject data into existing AF_IUCV connections, control the peer identity of accepted child sockets, and disrupt or kill established connections. Multiple Red Hat Enterprise Linux kernel and kernel-rt update streams and Red Hat In-Vehicle OS kernel streams are affected, and fixes are being pursued in the respective product streams; the kernel-ivos-qualcomm component of Red Hat In-Vehicle OS is not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in that kernel. The Red Hat severity of IMPORTANT (CVSS 3.1 score 7.0, AV:L/AC:H/PR:L) is lower than the upstream CVE.org rating of 8.1 (AV:A/AC:L/PR:N): Red Hat assessed the dominant exploitation path as local, requiring privileges and high attack complexity, whereas the upstream rating emphasizes the adjacent-network HiperSockets vector requiring no privileges. Note that AF_IUCV over HiperSockets provides no per-connection authentication, so the fix reduces the attack surface to peers present on the same HiperSockets segment but does not change that protocol-level property.

Prevent the nvme-tcp kernel module from loading if NVMe-over-TCP storage connectivity is not required on the host:

1. Create a configuration file to blacklist the driver and prevent it from loading:
# echo "install nvme-tcp /bin/true" > /etc/modprobe.d/nvme-tcp.conf
# echo "blacklist nvme-tcp" >> /etc/modprobe.d/nvme-tcp.conf

2. If the module is currently loaded, unload it:
# modprobe -r nvme-tcp

If the module is actively in use by mounted file systems or active block devices, it cannot be safely unloaded at runtime without first unmounting those targets, and a system reboot may be required to cleanly unload the driver.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's cx231xx media driver. A local attacker can exploit this vulnerability by manipulating video and Vertical Blanking Interval (VBI) queue operations. This allows for a heap out-of-bounds write, which could lead to arbitrary code execution or a denial of service.

notes.text: kernel: media: cx231xx: reject geometry changes while the VBI queue is busy
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has rated this Important severity flaw in the Linux kernel's cx231xx USB video capture (media) driver, affecting the kernel and kernel-rt packages in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 and 10 and in Red Hat In-Vehicle OS 2. The driver's vidioc_s_fmt_vid_cap() and vidioc_s_std() operations change device-wide geometry (dev->width / dev->norm) but only refuse the change when the video queue is busy. Because the VBI node shares those ioctl operations, a local attacker with access to the cx231xx device can allocate a small VBI videobuf2 plane and then enlarge dev->width or switch dev->norm through the video node while the VBI stream is running. cx231xx_do_vbi_copy() then recomputes the copy destination offset from the larger live geometry and memcpy()s device-delivered data past the end of the smaller, already allocated plane, producing a heap out-of-bounds write with an attacker-chosen offset. This kernel memory corruption can lead to privilege escalation, arbitrary code execution, or a system crash (denial of service). Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6, 7, and 8, including their kernel-rt builds, are not affected because the vulnerable code is not present in those kernels. Red Hat scores this flaw 7.0 (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), slightly lower than the upstream 7.8 score, because reliable exploitation requires precise manipulation of VBI queue geometry and device-delivered data in addition to local access to the video device. Fixes for the affected products are being pursued through the standard Red Hat update process.
